extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literature, especially those studying medieval/Renaissance poetry and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical observations for judging medieval and early-Renaissance literary works (poems, song-structures, short tales) with attention to aesthetic charm, historical/formative features, performance context, and thematic boldness. Emphasises how manner, detail, and emerging forms affect modern aesthetic appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic effect (manner over matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece 'aims at a purely artistic effect' and is to be 'entertained not for its matter only, but chiefly for its manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work's primary value comes from its style, form, and presentation rather than the plot or subject. Example: Aucassin and Nicolette treats a sorrowful subject yet presents it as 'a thing of joy and refreshment'—its manner transforms content. Anti-pattern: treating dramatic or tragic subject-matter as valuable solely for plot without regard to stylistic treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiquarian interest versus direct aesthetic charm
rubrics_metrics.description: An ancient composition may have 'antiquarian interest' (historical perspective) but this often 'means that it has no distinct aesthetic interest for the reader of to-day' unless it possesses 'a real, direct, aesthetic charm' in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish works whose value is primarily historical from those that still possess independent artistic merit. Scoring should penalize works that survive only as curiosities without intrinsic aesthetic qualities. Guidance: Antiquarian framing can enhance enjoyment only if the work contains genuine artistic qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity combined with refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: A desirable quality is the 'mixture of simplicity and refinement'—simple materials or forms handled with delicate, refined turns of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for apparently simple structures (e.g., short stanzas, plain plots) that are elevated by graceful phrasing, subtlety of tone, or refined perception. Example: the songs in Aucassin are 'of the simplest kind' yet show refined turns of expression. Anti-pattern: ornament without underlying simplicity; either crude simplicity or sophistication without clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid pictorial/detail work
rubrics_metrics.description: The work realizes scenes so fully that 'one still sees the ancient forest, with its disused roads grown deep with grass' and notices small, evocative details (garden, ruined tower, hut of flowers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the author's ability to create concrete, memorable images and small details that fix the reader's eye. Strong descriptive detail that supports mood and character is rewarded. Over-description that clutters or replaces narrative movement is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensory atmosphere (colour, smell, texture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Atmosphere is created via sensory cues: 'full-blown roses, the chamber painted... the cool brown marble, the almost nameless colours, the odour of plucked grass and flowers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score sensory richness and how effectively colour, smell, and tactile images sustain the work's mood. Positive examples are those that integrate sensory detail into characterization and setting rather than arbitrary listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character as embodiment of aesthetic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters like Nicolette are presented as embodiments of the work's aesthetic: 'the beautiful, weird, foreign girl' whose presence effects wonders and whose traits (knowledge of simples, healing touch) reinforce the poem's tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether characters are evocative, integrated with setting and theme, and whether their attributes serve poetic or symbolic functions. Avoid rewarding flat, purely expository character sketches that don't contribute to mood or theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance/contextual awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize original performative context: the piece 'was probably intended to be recited by a company of trained performers,' with rubrics like 'Or se cante' and 'Or dient et content et fabloient.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how awareness of performance, song, and rubrication affects structure and meaning. Evaluate staging cues, refrains, and the interplay of prose and song as intentional features. Anti-pattern: reading performative texts purely as static prose without accounting for song/practical performance elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative/emergent formal elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest often lies in the 'spectacle of the formation of a new artistic sense'—e.g., songs on the brink of true rhyme, 'always on the point of passing into true rhyme but... cannot quite take flight.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciate and evaluate embryonic or transitional formal features (incipient rhyme, hybrid prose-song forms) as historically and aesthetically significant. Reward sensitivity to innovation and nascent technique rather than demanding fully realized modern forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and musicality of language (assonance/rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: The early songs are 'not rhymed even, but only imperfectly assonant' with stanzas ending in similar vowel sounds; musical qualities matter even when full rhyme is absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge attention to sound—assonance, internal echoes, cadence—and how sound contributes to effect. Penalize prose that ignores musical effects when the genre historically relies upon them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charm in small turns of phrase / lightness and grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the piece's charm is 'in a turn of peculiar lightness and grace given to the situations and traits of sentiment' and in 'quaint fragments of early French prose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the felicity of phrasing: small epigrammatic turns, graceful micro-gestures in diction, and quaint idioms. Such turns can elevate otherwise simple scenes. Anti-pattern: overwrought rhetoric lacking these fine touches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend of humour/burlesque with serious sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The book 'has its burlesque element also' and alternates 'lighter matter' with 'morsels of a different quality'—serious, intense sentiment—so that humour and depth coexist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score a work's ability to balance comic/burlesque tones with genuine emotional intensity. Successful pieces use burlesque to accentuate or relieve seriousness rather than undermine core feeling. Anti-pattern: tonal inconsistency that collapses into parody or triviality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of intense, idealized passion
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative contains 'morsels of deeper colour, these expressions of the ideal intensity of love' (Aucassin's fainting, malady of love, physical traces of passion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate depiction of passion as an idealizing force—how physical effects and lyrical hyperbole convey intensity. Reward evocative, concentrated expressions of feeling; penalize flat or clinical accounts of emotion where lyric intensity is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative episodes chosen for their pictorial opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Adventures are 'of the simplest sort, adventures which seem to be chosen for the happy occasion they afford of keeping the eye of the fancy... fixed on pleasant objects.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plot and episode selection for their capacity to present evocative images and moments rather than for complexity of plot alone. In some genres, episodes function chiefly as tableaux; evaluate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of language and period flavour
rubrics_metrics.description: Value lies in 'quaint fragments of early French prose' and authentic linguistic turns that reflect period speech and idiom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score how convincingly the text evokes its linguistic era—through archaisms, idioms, and period-appropriate rhythm—without becoming unreadable. Avoid rewarding mere pastiche that lacks organic integration with content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic boldness: antinomian/rebellious elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A notable feature is the 'antinomianism, its spirit of rebellion and revolt against the moral and religious ideas of the time'—love as rival religion, pagan survivals, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate thematic courage in deviating from dominant moral frameworks and in exploring transgressive or heterodox impulses. Consider how the work negotiates or dramatizes such rebellion—whether it's thoughtful and integrated or merely sensational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of classical/pagan elements with Christian context
rubrics_metrics.description: Renaissance attempts to reconcile pagan gods and Greek thought with Christianity may produce allegorical readings and 'a general interest' when the synthesis is imaginatively achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how successfully a work weaves classical motifs into a Christian or contemporary moral framework, avoiding crude syncretism. Note when allegorical reinterpretation furthers aesthetic or intellectual aims; beware forced or strained reconciliations that misrepresent sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of cultured/audience specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Troubadour poetry 'wrote for an exclusive audience, people of much leisure and great refinement,' shaping content and tone accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work's registers, references, and modes of beauty align with its intended or implied audience. Differentiate between work meant for an elite cultivated circle and work aiming at broader accessibility; scoring should take audience expectations into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of narrative combined with evocative episodes (escape scene as exemplar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain short, well-rendered scenes (e.g., Nicolette's escape) are singled out as 'perhaps the prettiest passage in the whole piece'—short episodes can exemplify the work's strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give credit for compact, self-contained episodes that achieve high poetic effect and advance tone; judge the economy of narration that nevertheless yields vivid scenes.
